builtBy: qa-engineer (hand-read from the rendered page PNGs in data/accuracy/manuals/<id>/pages; regions read off the 1600 px images)
notes: sourceSha256 is the hash of the rendered PDF (data/accuracy/manuals/anavi-thermometer/manual.pdf); the Markdown hash is 5b969ced7b6fe80927f8f5bb078e1d61861dcf9e574ec140d7d47b429cd5f0df. The layout is ours (A4, DejaVu Sans, 11 pt), 9 pages, so this manual tests text extraction, step order and warnings, not diagram location: every region is a block of text. The manual has no pictures. It is mostly prose: the "steps" are its procedures (configure, reset, flash, OTA, home-automation), keyed in manual order. Things deliberately NOT keyed as steps: the five optional sensor wiring tables (4 Dupont wires, pins VCC/VIN, GND, SCL, SDA to 3.3V/GND/SCL/SDA), the pinout and I2C chapters, the FAQ and the revision history. Tools named: screwdriver ("bare hands and a screwdriver"), grounding strap or similar protective device. Printed numbers a model may legitimately use: 5V, 1A (1000mA), 6 seconds, 2 seconds, 4M (1M SPIFFS), 75 mm x 40 mm, 3 I2C slots, 4 Dupont wires, 4.7kohm R2/R3, ports 1883 and 8080, and the library version list. The manual has typos that must be reproduced, not corrected: "Arudino", "It very important", "Be sure the back up", "AM2303" next to "AM2302".
tools: grounding strap or similar protective device

steps.summary: Add sensors, optionally assemble the acrylic case, and plug the 5V supply into the microUSB port.
Power on, connect to the temporary WiFi access point, choose your WiFi network and MQTT settings, copy the machine ID and click save.
steps.ambiguityNote: Prose, not numbered, running from the bottom of page 3 to the top of page 4; steps 2 and 3 may be merged by a model.

steps.summary: Verify the device at demo.anavi.technology by entering the machine ID and clicking connect.
steps.ambiguityNote: Two sentences at the top of page 4 that follow the configuration text; may be merged into the configuration step.

steps.summary: Reset to factory defaults by holding the button for about 6 seconds until the red light stops blinking.
Set up the Arduino IDE: install it, add the ESP8266 board package, select the board and flash size, and add the listed libraries.
steps.ambiguityNote: Five numbered sub-steps plus a 13-item library list; a model may split it into several steps or keep one.

steps.summary: Flash custom firmware: select the module settings, load a sketch, compile, connect the USB-to-serial board, upload while holding RESET.
steps.ambiguityNote: Seven numbered sub-steps split across pages 4 and 5; may be one step or several.

steps.summary: Check whether the firmware supports OTA by sending the MQTT message "test" to cmnd/[deviceId]/line1.
Enable OTA upgrades with an OTA server entry in the captive portal or by defining OTA_SERVER in the source.
Build the binary: use Sketch > Export compiled binary and copy the .bin file to the web server.
Trigger the update by sending a JSON message with file and server to cmnd/[deviceid]/update.
steps.ambiguityNote: Runs from the bottom of page 5 onto page 6.

steps.summary: Optionally use signed builds: generate a key pair with openssl and use the .bin.signed file.
steps.ambiguityNote: Optional ("strongly encouraged"), not a required step.

steps.summary: Change the temperature scale with the MQTT message to cmnd/machine-id/tempformat and a JSON scale payload.
Integrate with Home Assistant using the MQTT sensor component or MQTT Discovery in configuration.yaml.
steps.ambiguityNote: Starts at the bottom of page 6 and continues on page 7.

steps.summary: OpenHAB step 1: install the MQTT Binding add-on in Paper UI.
OpenHAB step 2: add and configure the MQTT Broker thing and check it is online.
OpenHAB step 3: install the JavaScript Transformation add-on.
OpenHAB step 4: download temperature.js and humidity.js into $OPENHAB_CONF/transform.
OpenHAB step 5: add the thermometer as a Generic MQTT Thing with temperature and humidity channels.
steps.ambiguityNote: Runs over the page break between pages 7 and 8.

warnings.text: ANAVI Thermometer is shipped in a protective bag. It must NOT be exposed to high electrostatic potentials. A grounding strap or similar protective device should be worn when handling the board. Avoid touching the component pins or any other metallic element.
Make sure that you are using a 5V power supply from a trusted supplier. Cheap, untested power supplies can be risky and unreliable.
It very important to copy the machine ID. Later it is needed to identify your device.
warnings.ambiguityNote: Plain sentence, not formatted as a warning; it is a critical instruction. Reproduced with the manual's own grammar ("It very important").

warnings.text: Note: Issues might be experienced if using different versions of the libraries.
Note: you have to be quick between step 5 and 6. Remember to press and hold RESET until the upload completes.

The web server can be located anywhere, but for improved security it is best if it is located on your local network, and no untrusted persons should be able to edit any files at all on the server. Don't host your firmware images on a shared server!
Note: to ensure a successful update, please specify the file with leading slash ('/'), use an HTTP web server, not HTTPS, and -- when run from the command line -- escape quote characters

Note: After the update, you may find that readings from the DHT22 sensor no longer work and temperature and humidity are shown as "0". In this case, please powercycle the device (unplug power until display turns off, then plug power in again)
Be sure the back up the private.key file, and make sure nobody can get hold of it.
IMPORTANT NOTE: In both topics replace <workgroup> and <machine id> with valid values!
